payload.title: Windows drive-relative resolution uses ambient CWD despite explicit base
payload.summary: P2 path-policy correctness. On native Windows, resolve_path("C:relative.txt", base_directory=Path("Z:/explicit-base")) returns a path under current C-drive CWD. Changing only CWD between two real temporary directories changes the result with identical supplied input/base. Relative inputs are documented/tested as explicit-base operations independent of ambient CWD. Native cross-drive joining drops the supplied base before Path.resolve. Same-drive, rooted-current-drive and fully absolute Windows forms must be separately specified. This is a public primitive policy defect, not proof of an agent authorization bypass.
payload.benefit: Reject incompatible drive-relative input with the existing path-domain error before CWD-dependent normalization, or obtain an explicit equally deterministic supported policy. Preserve ordinary relative/absolute paths, missing targets, native case/link normalization and no-containment semantics. Independent Windows tests hold input/base fixed while changing CWD and establish refusal or identical explicit results. Same-drive drive-relative and rooted inputs require controls. Repository Tool/RI/Checkout callers must retain their own scope/alias checks; do not create another path resolver or promise TOCTOU elimination.
payload.uncertainty: Public resolve_path is affected. Current observed Qwen/RI/Checkout callers add path-address/alias/root checks, so no current untrusted task escape is established. UNC shares, redirected drives and junction races were not exercised. Core path policy is the existing owner; repair requires bounded later authorization.
dependencies: Existing owner/API contracts; separately authorized bounded production repair; independent permanent regressions and full unchanged protected validation.
